family.tagline: A house full of sensors and a teen who builds things.
family.story: Rosa is a self-employed solar installer who writes her quotes at the dining table. Kari teaches science, and Idris builds robots. They share one table and one Companion Core.

companion.name: Dalia
companion.job: Drafts site-visit notes and quote cover letters from what Rosa texts it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Rosa sends every quote.

companion.name: Wick
companion.job: Drafts parts lists and build notes for the robotics club from Idris's texts.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Idris decides what to build.

popup.title: A parcel on the timber steps
popup.body: A parcel sits on the broad timber steps, between the tropical beds. Idris carries it through the entry hall to the sunroom lounge.

popup.title: Kari unpacks the parcel
popup.body: Kari unpacks the parcel: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. The Core covers about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Idris plugs it in
popup.body: Idris plugs in the power cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Rosa joins from her phone
popup.body: Rosa joins the Core's own Wi-Fi from her phone. Then she picks the home network from the list and enters its password.

popup.title: Two agents, three apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Rosa and Idris each pick Hermes. They add Home Assistant, DocuSeal and Pi-hole, plus Companion Memory (beta). Then they walk away.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Wick says hello
popup.body: Idris texts the agent he named Wick. Wick answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: idris
say.text: Hello, Idris. Wick here. What are we building?

beats.capability: Listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off on any device

popup.title: Grading to a podcast
popup.body: Kari catches up on a science podcast in Audiobookshelf while she grades. The episodes live on the Core and pick up where she left off.

beats.capability: Design a Home Assistant dashboard by dragging widgets, with no YAML

popup.title: A dashboard, built by dragging
popup.body: Idris drags widgets into a GlassHome dashboard, with no YAML. It shows what the family's own sensors read through Home Assistant.

beats.capability: Block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: What the house asks the internet
popup.body: Kari opens Pi-hole and reads which domains the house asked for this morning. It blocks ad and tracker domains at DNS for every device.

beats.capability: Keep your own searchable archive of web pages

popup.title: A reading list that stays put
popup.body: Kari saves the pages she teaches from in ArchiveBox. Her own searchable archive sits on the Core, ready for next term.

beats.capability: A shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner and expense tracker for the household

popup.title: Meals planned at the breakfast bar
popup.body: Kari plans the week's meals in KitchenOwl at the breakfast bar. Idris adds his ride snacks, and the list syncs to every phone.

beats.capability: Track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: Subscriptions, listed and reviewed
popup.body: Kari lists the household subscriptions in Wallos. It reminds her before each renewal, and she decides what to keep.

beats.capability: A family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals, notes, contacts and budget in one

popup.title: Three schedules, one calendar
popup.body: Rosa adds her site-visit days to Yuvomi's shared calendar. They sit beside Kari's school term and Idris's club nights.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Dalia drafts the cover letter
popup.body: Rosa texts Dalia her site notes. Dalia drafts the cover letter from context in Companion Memory, and Rosa reads it and sends it herself.

say.speaker: rosa
say.text: Draft ready. Please read it first.

beats.capability: Fill and sign PDF forms on any device, from your own Core

popup.title: Signed at the dining table
popup.body: A customer stops by to sign. Rosa fills in the quote form in DocuSeal, and the customer signs on a tablet at the table.

beats.capability: Keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: Every customer, first call to quote
popup.body: Rosa tracks each customer in Twenty, from first call to signed quote, with custom fields of her own. The CRM runs on the Core.

beats.capability: Invoicing, expenses, customers and profit and loss for a small business

popup.title: The month's books, in one place
popup.body: Rosa enters the month's expenses in Akaunting. Invoices, customers and the profit and loss report all sit together on the Core.

beats.capability: Archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them

popup.title: Warranty papers, filed and waiting
popup.body: Rosa files each customer's contract and warranty papers in Papra. They wait on the Core until someone asks for them.

beats.capability: Model low-poly 3D art and Minecraft-style models in your browser

popup.title: Robots at the other end
popup.body: Quotes at one end of the table, robots at the other. Idris sketches his next robot's body in Blockbench to check its shape.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Wick drafts the parts list
popup.body: The robotics club needs a parts list. Idris texts Wick his build notes, and Wick drafts it. Idris checks every line and orders the parts himself.

say.speaker: idris
say.text: Parts list drafted. Please check it before you order.

beats.capability: Track runs, rides and gear and see your fitness stats on your own server

popup.title: The commute, kept on the Core
popup.body: Idris adds his morning commute to Endurain as a GPX file. His rides and his bicycle gear are tracked on the Core.

beats.capability: Track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: The raised beds have a journal
popup.body: Kari logs the raised beds in HortusFox, bed by bed, with watering notes and photos. The journal grows with the season.

beats.capability: Control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: The soil sensor reports in
popup.body: A soil sensor in the raised beds reports to Home Assistant over the home Wi-Fi. Rosa checks the reading on the dashboard before she waters.

popup.title: Quotes, robots and one Core
popup.body: The Vasquez-Nilsen family runs quotes at one end of the table and robots at the other. Both run from one Companion Core.

closing.body: Keep your quotes, your contracts and your sensor readings on a Companion Core at home. Robots at one end of the table, paperwork at the other.

notes: FTUE follows the owner-specified hotspot flow; the fact sheet says only "plug it in, pair it over Wi-Fi, and walk away". Owner sign-off open.

No living-room TV: the media beat is an Audiobookshelf podcast at the couch. Energy care: Home Assistant and GlassHome beats say only what sensors read on the home network; no energy figure, saving or solar claim.
Both companions are Hermes, so ftue-hello carries the Hermes note. dining-quote uses Companion Memory (Dalia has it connected, opt-in).
dining-sign: the customer signs on a tablet on the home Wi-Fi at the table; no remote signer and no legal claim. DocuSeal listing says signers outside the home network need access to the Core.

living-dashboard and garden-soil assume the family owns sensors on the home network; none is in the Core parcel. Endurain: GPX upload only, no Strava or Garmin sync. Blockbench is low-poly modelling; check the robot-body wording.
